role: Business Intelligence Engineer, SCOT - Automated Inventory Management
responsibilities: Performing complex analysis to understand the behavior of automated inventory management systems, identify the root cause of system / process issues and provide insight on potential solutions.
Building audits (analytical products) to identify trend breaks or defects at scale for millions of products and multiple Marketplaces globally
Assessing the end-to-end suite of audits and identifying opportunities for enhancements and simplification, working with other audit owners

Creating new solutions to automate the business process of identifying and resolving defects (e.g. through metric dashboards and automated alarms, self service dashboard, Single source of truth tables... )
Supporting the improvement of the automated audit workflow system: integrating new audits and providing input on the future developments/roadmap
Fostering culture of continuous engineering improvement through blueprints, mentoring, feedback, and metrics

evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: Building audits (analytical products) to identify trend breaks or defects at scale for millions of products
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: The JD centers on building audits, detecting defects, and ensuring accuracy of inventory systems with no velocity/speed language, coding as rigour.
evidence.domain_risk: we decide what, when, where, and how much we should buy to meet Amazon's business goals... hundreds of product lines worth billions of dollars of inventory world-wide
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: Errors affect large-scale operational inventory decisions worth billions of dollars but the JD's language is about operational auditing and defect detection, not financial reporting or regulatory compliance, so moderate despite the scale.
